title: Readings in distributed systems
abstract: No abstract or summary section is provided in the HTML document.
summary:
This document is a work-in-progress curated reading list rather than a conventional research paper. It organizes influential distributed-systems literature into consensus, consistency, conflict-free data structures, distributed programming, systems, and books. The author explicitly includes both successful systems and techniques and ideas that were later dismissed or shown to be incorrect, emphasizing the historical progression of concepts. ([christophermeiklejohn.com](https://christophermeiklejohn.com/distributed/systems/2013/07/12/readings-in-distributed-systems.html))

The list has been reused as a resource in distributed-systems education and in other curated collections. Aphyr’s distributed-systems course materials identify it as a source of key papers, while Papers We Love catalogs it as a distributed-systems reading resource. ([github.com](https://github.com/aphyr/distsys-class)) It is also referenced by distributed-systems meta-lists and “awesome” resource collections. ([gitextract.com](https://gitextract.com/theanalyst/awesome-distributed-systems)) No evidence was found that the document itself introduced a research result or directly influenced an identifiable line of academic research; its documented impact is primarily as a secondary educational and bibliographic resource.
